newsitem.title: UKRAINE: NAZI MINES FOUND UNDER UKRAINE SOCCER FIELD.
newsitem.headline: NAZI MINES FOUND UNDER UKRAINE SOCCER FIELD.

text.p: Three mines placed by Nazi forces during World War Two have been found under a soccer pitch where a week ago the German and Ukrainian under-21 teams played, a spokesman for the stadium said on Friday.
"The mines have been in the ground for at least 55 years. They were German. It is an echo of the war," Olexiy Semenenko, a spokesman for Dynamo stadium, said.

Semenenko said the three anti-infantry mines had been discovered about 1.5 metres (yards) beneath the field during modernisation work late on Thursday. They were removed and detonated on the outskirts of Kiev.
Dynamo Kiev, Ukraine's top soccer club, usually play at the 40,000-seat stadium in the heart of the capital of the former Soviet republic.
The last match at the stadium was a World Cup qualifying match between the under-21 sides while the senior teams played on Saturday June 7 at the bigger Olympic stadium in Kiev.
